clue.text: Problem solvable when characters first come together?

definitions.text: Problem solvable when characters first come together?

parts.words: Problem solvable when characters first come together?
parts.note: a word puzzle in which the opening letters of successive lines, read down together, spell out a hidden word

explanation.surface: A mystery story that only resolves when all the main characters finally meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people in a story, but here they are letters, and 'first' means the initial letters of each line.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of puzzle or poem has its line-initial letters spelling a word, so it is solved when those first letters are joined.

clue.text: See military officer impede a cad misbehaving

indicators.note: behaving badly means the letters are disorderly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A staff officer is seen obstructing a cad who is behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misbehaving' rearranges IMPEDE A CAD; 'See' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an officer who acts as a personal assistant to a senior commander.

clue.text: Increase speed, seeing vicar?

definitions.meaning: to ... an engine is to make it turn faster
Short for Reverend, the title of a vicar

explanation.surface: A clergyman puts his foot down.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: revving an engine speeds it, and the abbreviated clerical title belongs to a vicar.

clue.text: Jazz musician who's nominated — is doing a roll

indicators.note: rolling over turns the run upside down, so in a down clue the letters read backwards

parts.note: nominated means named
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jazz player nominated for an award is on a roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a roll' reverses NAMED + IS to give SI DEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporting player in a jazz band, not the leader, is a sideman.

clue.text: Bing endlessly reliving end of December —- mushy originator of White Christmas

indicators.note: something mushy is pulped, so these letters are mashed up
without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: picks the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Bing Crosby keeps reliving a sentimental December, recalling the song's composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims Bing to BIN, 'end of December' gives R, and 'mushy' rearranges BIN + RELIVING + R.
explanation.definitionFit: The songwriter composed the classic festive song made famous by Bing Crosby.

clue.text: Affectionate term for imp, ever a scallywag? Only partly

indicators.note: Only partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fond nickname for a mischievous child who has always been a little scamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a naughty child a little scamp or rogue is a fond, teasing usage of this word.

clue.text: Bubble chamber?

parts.note: a pocket of trapped gas blocking a pipe, or a sealed compartment between areas of different pressure

explanation.surface: A physicist's particle detector.
explanation.walkthrough: A bubble chamber is a particle detector, but here 'bubble' is a gas pocket and 'chamber' a sealed compartment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a blockage caused by a bubble of air in a pipe and an airtight chamber.

clue.text: Kit is in short supply for this boy

definitions.text: Kit is in short supply for this boy

parts.words: Kit is in short supply for this boy
parts.note: Kit is a shortened pet form of a certain boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad's equipment is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kit' reads as equipment and 'in short supply' as scarce, but Kit is short for the boy's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit is a familiar diminutive of this traditional boy's name.

clue.text: Machine cut strip of wood

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a lathe is a machine for turning wood or metal

explanation.surface: A machine slices a strip of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of LATHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lath is a thin narrow strip of wood used in walls and trellises.

clue.text: American branches, etc, produced repeated payout

indicators.note: says the word for a payout is written out twice in a row

parts.note: a divi is an informal British word for a dividend, a share-out of profits

explanation.surface: A US company's branch offices keep paying out dividends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American branches, etc' is a whimsical way of describing a tropical American tree by its parts; 'branches' misleads toward company offices.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical American tree of the pea family, whose pods yield tannin, is here described through its branches and other parts.

clue.text: Boring rubbish -—- it may make one's beam disappear

definitions.text: it may make one's beam disappear

parts.note: dull or tedious means dry
nonsense or rubbish is rot

explanation.surface: Tedious nonsense that wipes the smile off your face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' reads as a broad smile, but it is a wooden timber, which fungal decay can destroy.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungal decay attacks structural timber, so a wooden beam can crumble away completely.

clue.text: Fascist who could be lawless and moody

indicators.note: says the letters could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fascist who might be lawless and sullen.
explanation.walkthrough: OSWALD MOSLEY led the British Union of Fascists in the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: He founded and led Britain's leading fascist movement before the Second World War.

clue.text: Oxford couples welcoming the patiently ambitious?

definitions.text: Oxford couples welcoming the patiently ambitious?

parts.words: Oxford couples welcoming the patiently ambitious?
parts.note: pairs of Oxford footwear left vacant for those who wait for a superior to die so they can take over the job

explanation.surface: Pairs at Oxford University welcome students who are ambitious but patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the university, but oxfords are lace-up shoes; the phrase means a post you only get when its holder dies.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a position or inheritance obtainable only after the current holder dies, which patient careerists wait for.

clue.text: One gauges intensity of performance, mostly oddly remote

indicators.note: most of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: acting is performance

indicators.note: behaving oddly means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A device measuring how intense a performance is, mostly remotely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ACTING to ACTIN; 'oddly' rearranges REMOTE to OMETER.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures the intensity of radiation, especially of sunlight.

clue.text: What loss-making turf accountant did is a mystery

definitions.meaning: a bookmaker (turf accountant) losing money shut up shop and stopped taking bets

explanation.surface: Why a struggling bookmaker went under is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: A turf accountant is a British euphemism for a bookmaker who takes bets on horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one knows nothing about is likened to a shut volume, while a failing bookie stops accepting bets.

clue.text: Interrupt, offering copper money

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone breaks into a conversation to offer some coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt into a conversation or a dance partnership is a phrasal verb meaning to interrupt.

clue.text: Northern football team angry before game

parts.note: a black look or mood is an angry one
pool is a cue game played on a table

explanation.surface: A northern English football side, furious before a match.
explanation.walkthrough: BLACKPOOL is a seaside town in north-west England whose football club is known as the Seasiders.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club from the Lancashire seaside resort plays in the north of England.

clue.text: Fellow healed, one admitted and given quick treatment?

indicators.note: one being let in between the other two pieces means placed inside them

parts.note: a fellow is a man
healed means cured
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man is healed after being admitted to hospital and seen quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' suggests speed, but the quick is the tender flesh under a fingernail, so quick treatment is nail care.
explanation.definitionFit: Having one's nails and hands trimmed and polished is treatment of the fingertips, where the quick lies.

clue.text: Clash badly when turning up to break the rules

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: a code is a set of rules

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: badly means ill

explanation.surface: Things go wrong when someone shows up and breaks the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' means reading from bottom to top; 'to break' signals the reversed piece breaking into the rule set.
explanation.definitionFit: To collide is to clash or crash together.

clue.text: Musketeer's mount

definitions.meaning: one of the three musketeers in Dumas's novel, with the 's standing for is
a holy mountain in north-east Greece, home to many monasteries

explanation.surface: A musketeer's horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' reads as a horse a musketeer rides, but it is a mountain in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a Dumas swordsman and to the Greek monastic peninsula's mountain.

clue.text: Passionate, taking a second to get going — never ending!

parts.note: mo is short for a moment, a second

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to rouse is to stir into action

explanation.surface: A passionate person takes a moment to warm up, then never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never ending' trims ROUSE to ROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amorous means full of passionate or romantic desire.

clue.text: End of the turmoil, cloud disperses as rainbow appears

indicators.note: scattering in all directions signals that these letters are rearranged
picks only the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: After a storm, the cloud breaks up and a rainbow shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of the' gives E; 'disperses' scatters E with TURMOIL and CLOUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, rainbow describes something of many bright colours, a synonym here.

clue.text: Incomplete imitation shown up? Sorry!

indicators.note: in a down clue, shown up means the letters read upwards
not complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a spoof is a parody or imitation

explanation.surface: An unfinished impersonation is exposed, and the performer apologises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incomplete' trims SPOOF to SPOO; 'shown up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is an apology uttered after a small blunder.

clue.text: Be too clever for Oxford University nincompoop

parts.note: a fool or nincompoop is a twit

explanation.surface: A university fool is outsmarted.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsmart or outmanoeuvre someone is to beat them by greater cunning.

clue.text: Place that could be loaded with gold stashed away

indicators.note: hidden inside, so one piece goes within the other
says the letters of the next word could be rearranged into something else

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Somewhere that might be filled with hidden gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' shuffles the six letters of the clue word into ELDADO; 'stashed away' hides the heraldic gold inside that scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of gold sought in South America is a fabled place of riches.

clue.text: Chief officer once more leaving home

indicators.note: one piece departs from the other, so it is removed

parts.note: once more means again
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: The chief officer again leaves his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes IN out of AGAIN; an aga was a Turkish military commander.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga was a commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: County right to give way to very formal inspection

indicators.note: one letter yields its place to another, so it is replaced

parts.note: SURREY is a county south of London

explanation.surface: A county's rights yield to a very formal examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give way to' swaps the second R of SURREY for V.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal survey is an official examination or inspection of land or a building.

clue.text: Attachment shown by beast on the lookout?

definitions.text: Attachment shown by beast on the lookout?

parts.words: Attachment shown by beast on the lookout?
parts.note: a crab or snail has its organs of sight mounted on a movable stem, an appendage that helps it watch

explanation.surface: A watchful animal shows its fondness for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attachment' suggests affection, but here it is a body part attached to the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs and snails carry their eyes on stalks, a physical attachment used for looking out.
